question: GQ-001
subject: the items that passed the guards were worse than the ones that failed
the_symptom: a batch of 200 returned 123 OK and 77 failures — 76 of the 77 were manuscript letters (William Cheyney to his son, 1891-1894)

the_worse_half.what: THIRTEEN letters PASSED the NO_TEXT and BAD_BODY guards and entered the corpus
the_worse_half.their_text: OCR of handwriting — "Pivincelsne aerate", "ieledelbia", "Dhiledilthi" for Philadelphia
the_worse_half.why_no_gate_caught_them: they score 0.541 and 0.547 on the English-dictionary check, ABOVE the 0.45 threshold, because printed letterhead (OFFICE, COMPANY, STREET) carries them past it
the_worse_half.consequence: corpus-integrity does not catch these and never would have

the_filter.pattern: Letter(s) to/from ... <year> — requires a YEAR, not merely the word "letter"
the_filter.why: Vegetable Growers' News Letter is a printed periodical and must survive

validated_against_two_real_manifests.note: all 13 are Cheyney letters that should be skipped too — zero real books excluded

result.remaining_letter_titles: 2, both printed 18th-century pamphlets (A letter to Thomas Trotter : occasioned by his proposal)

a_reading_i_had_to_correct: I first read the 13 as "real books the filter would discard" and nearly abandoned it. Opening their text showed they were the same manuscripts — the trade was never 13 books against 87 wasted fetches.
